phases.objective: Bind every GitHub repository provider write to the exact repo_patch_apply capability key while preserving existing app, intent, resource, commit, approval, and dispatch guards.

e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: A GitHub write with repo_patch_apply is authorized only when the envelope capability key, app key, intent, resource, commit, and dispatch state all match; a different capability key is rejected before provider transport.
steps: Construct a repository write envelope with the GitHub app key and repo_patch_apply capability key.
Validate the exact repository resource, branch, expected commit, dispatch, approval, blocking-gap, and secret-free constraints.
Allow the provider write only after the complete envelope resolves successfully.
Construct an otherwise valid envelope with a different capability key.
Reject the mismatched capability before any provider request is sent.
assertions: The GitHub write boundary passes acceptedCapabilityKeys=[repo_patch_apply] to the envelope resolver.
A capability key other than repo_patch_apply returns capability_resolution_envelope_capability_mismatch.
Capability mismatch produces zero provider transport calls.
Existing accepted app and operation-intent allowlists remain enforced.
Existing resource, commit, readiness, dispatch, approval, blocking-gap, and no-secret guards remain enforced.
The regression is exercised through the public authority-checked lifecycle module rather than the unguarded core module.

phases.objective: Observe the exact capability-key contract in governed non-production repository mutation operations without broadening provider or database authority.
Reconcile capability envelope and repository authority evidence after source, branch, or commit drift.
Validate one non-production repository mutation surface with the exact capability key and no provider transport on mismatch.
Verify production readback only after separately authorized deployment and exact-head validation.
